newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet firm on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet firm on short covering.

text.p: Asian jet fuel swaps market firmed late afternoon on Monday on short covering of physical cargoes by traders, industry sources said.
The December jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) rose in the afternoon and was last quoted at $2.10/$2.30 a barrel, up from this morning's $1.90, brokers said.
Traders said that the hike was due to higher physical cargo prices due to short covering by traders.
One cargo traded on Friday at a premium of close to $2.00 a barrel over spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, up about 20 cents from the previous deal, traders said.
In the Singapore physical market, a bid by a major for 120,000-barrels at $32.30 a barrel fob on Friday, up 35 cents from Thursday's traded post-winter high, failed to find sellers.
December gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon and were last quoted at $30.55/$30.70. It traded earlier in the day at $30.63, brokers said.
The December/January backwardation widened slightly due to tight prompt physical supplies and was quoted notionally at 60/70 cents, brokers said.
January gas oil was seen slightly weaker relative to December due in part to the lower than expected Indian diesel purchase for January, brokers said.
January swaps traded earlier in the day at $29.90 a barrel.

India bought in a tender a modest 255,000-tonnes of diesel for delivery in January down from initial expectations of 700,000 tonnes and also lower than the late Friday expectations of 350,000 tonnes, brokers said.

Traders said the market was supported by tight December supplies from regional sources. As a result, Chinese buyers are paying up to $249 a tonne for small lots sold on an ex-terminal basis in Hong Kong.
Offers to China for cargoes are at around $239 a tonne cost-and freight south China with firm bids about $3-$4 less, traders said.
Physical gas oil in Singapore was bid on Friday to a new five-year of $31.00 a barrel free-on-board. Sellers were sidelined because of tight prompt supplies, traders said.
Naphtha was unchanged from midday. December was last bid at $23.30 with no firm sellers seen, brokers said, from Friday's $23.55/$23.70.
Fuel oil swaps were little changed in a quiet market. December was last quoted at $119.50/$121.25 a tonne.
